chemistry_scientist.state_summary: Round 1 reports 365 measured records, including all 32 previous acquisitions, and 2965 eligible candidates; none are pending. The new measurements strengthen graph-specific quinoline and injection-solvent questions, support conditional loading responses, and resolve several historical prediction anomalies. Current predictions have changed substantially. Historical premeasurement errors and current predictions must remain distinct. The objective remains overall Row V1/V2 accuracy after retraining.
important_observations: H_load, revised: measured loading responses depend on eluent and endpoint. For m8 at 1/1, 78.65, 157.3 and 235.95 mg give V1/V2 5.32/9.45, 4.23/11.45 and 4.22/13.04 mL (fd0fd67502640304b8fb; a98f3e4664fd05c0f82c; 6c4ddf5ad1cf067b81ee). At 5/1, 78.65 versus 157.3 mg gives 5.74/11.29 versus 4.72/14.07 (c8176b3eea7a5d8802dc; 898bde0c214429571108). These support widening with loading locally.

H_load, limits: m92 at 1/1 with EA loading changes from 5.18/12.01 to 6.29/9.73 mL when mass increases from 57.75 to 173.25 mg (00a89de0e6cc7377a84b; 4451265787d29526a93a), opposing a universal widening rule. At 50/1 the same loads give 22.57/52.44 and 20.51/62.21 (1844eab177de5d01fab6; 9bbd36c8b484b5609808). At 10/1 the intermediate 115.5 mg result, 8.85/28.15 (4b8ba288d549f6cfc94b), exceeds both low- and high-load V2 anchors, 21.03 and 24.51 mL. This establishes a recorded nonmonotone sequence, not a smooth adsorption law.

H_load, reproducibility and transfer: the m44 high-load repeat gives 7.76/20.25 mL (61d5633c7221b3040a5f), compared with the first high-load result 9.85/20.92 (18d688363c7fa3da0609) and low-load result 11.88/17.52 (4d75c120ba1c4f0dae89). The opposing endpoint shift survives, with appreciable onset variation. For m101 at 2/1, approximately 50 versus 150 mg gives 4.32/12.10 and 4.93/12.82 (2f95389e141635b0e27c; e48a024ed5f697067195), a weaker completion response than its measured 1/1 contrast.

H_ratio, split into local questions: m173 at fixed mass and DCM 2000 uL has V2 108.89, 45.06 and 60.92 mL at 1/1, 2/1 and 5/1 (f90a5a5a54509c085ebd; 0b247863fd6e8aaf44d8; 1e775e7d8dcbf48fd6f8). m73's measured sequence is 18.60/18.96 at 1/1, 5.26/11.60 at 2/1, 5.63/13.55 at 5/1 and 9.59/28.68 at 50/1 at essentially matched mass and injection setup (2cf789c87f7c6325c020; 49932dbd3d16bb64f71a; c9a9fab963b85f141aa6; e6dcf9d6f65fa598a38e). Its unusual 1/1 result is localized relative to the subsequent progression. For m80, matched 105.5 mg measurements give 4.08/15.66 at 1/1 and 6.41/8.27 at 50/1 (55dfd30fde788076a355; 08155ffdcb0d27576050). Earlier completion at weaker eluent survives removal of the previous loading confound.

H_nitrogen, supported specifically for quinoline transfer: at fixed loading, changing 1/1 to 5/1 moves m146 from 13.28/23.85 to 37.67/59.83 mL (b6229f0445560a4a54ed; 04a2e8ad27ca641a3a12), and m216 from 11.59/23.93 to 31.43/56.33 (d1e71a8278523e7a10e3; 1ae3618ec277b0463686). Historical 5/1 errors were -27.84/-32.47 and -20.35/-28.90 mL. Conversely, para-aminobenzonitrile m160 was predicted closely at 2/1; measured endpoints exceed the matched meta isomer by only 0.29/2.26 mL (2feb7d8e0a3566ddf97f; 53a1acff30433cff819f). A generic nitrogen correction is unsupported.

H_injection, supported for one solvent contrast: m92 at 1/1, 57.75 mg and a 200 uL plug changes from 5.18/12.01 with EA loading to 8.02/20.57 with PE loading (00a89de0e6cc7377a84b; e626b5b8083ea1fd02f2). For m173 at 2/1, reducing DCM from 2000 to 1500 uL changes onset by -0.025 mL and completion by +1.16 mL, with a 0.05 mg mass difference (0b247863fd6e8aaf44d8; 9a32b65bc21fdc5f7286). The latter supplies little evidence for a large plug effect at that ratio. Neither contrast establishes a general causal effect without replication.

H_onset, specific question resolved: m177 at 10/1 and 140.6 mg measures 5.20/20.70 mL (ce14dd2481560a984aea), close to its matched 5/1 onset of 5.06 (08812206a257481691c4). The historical zero-onset prediction failed at this condition. m126 at 20/1 measures an ordered interval, 6.21/11.84 (87814eeffb35c15f3f89), contradicting its historical reversed prediction. The causes remain unidentified.

Additional measured transfer evidence: m91 gives narrow intervals, 5.62/7.98 at 2/1 and 7.29/11.12 at 5/1 (d603d4af5fd62fa8b85e; a2ecf2b2f28094d70368); historical predictions placed onset too early and completion too late. In contrast, m82 at 10/1 measures 20.41/45.62 with both endpoints historically underpredicted (6b8e53d2d8c8a90a7216). Sulfoxide m199 measures 12.32/22.67 at 2/1 versus historical 4.34/12.45 (b060fa3ae84f80e773d2). Alcohol m60 measures 19.65/34.70 at 5/1, much later than benzylic m61 at 10.27/15.56 under near-matched PE loading protocols (62d7ea74ab73fa6214b4; 994a1f65509549a84ede). Close cyclic-ketone transfer to m180 was comparatively accurate (73a35f890e678b320073).
important_model_behaviors: CURRENT PREDICTIONS: loading sensitivity remains tiny. For m92 at 10/1, 57.75 versus 173.25 mg predicts 9.903/23.806 versus 9.905/23.814 mL (0389a6366b3a51fad8b5; ad0ace61c29817c678c2). These physical inputs already have measurements; this comparison diagnoses training fit and feature sensitivity, not prospective accuracy.

CURRENT PREDICTIONS: some new curves turn downward beyond measured long-retention anchors. At matched mass, m216 at 10/1 predicts 29.58/44.53, preceding its measured 5/1 endpoints 31.43/56.33. m82 at 20/1 predicts 15.36/37.98, preceding its measured 10/1 endpoints 20.41/45.62. These are untested response shapes, not demonstrated candidate errors.

CURRENT QUANTILES: ordering defects persist. d997636736faa38ac83a has V1 q10/q50/q90 approximately 3.39/5.96/3.40 mL despite a positive reported quantile width. Small numerical widths do not establish confidence.

Where do m92's loading response and m80's unusual completion response change with eluent?
Does the new quinoline information transfer to a pyridyl ketone, and do current weak-eluent predictions preserve the measured molecular distinctions?

particularly_informative_candidates.question: m92 at 2/1, EA 200 uL, 57.75 versus 173.25 mg; both predict approximately 4.43/10.63 mL. A controlled loading contrast at a missing ratio tests where the observed response changes sign.

m73 at 1/1, 104.91 mg, DCM 300 uL predicts 11.42/17.15 mL. This nearly repeats observed 2cf789c87f7c6325c020, differing by only 0.01 mg, and directly examines reproducibility of the late, narrow interval.
m80 at 105.5 mg, PE 200 uL: 10/1 predicts 10.68/21.53 and 20/1 predicts 7.06/14.25 mL. These alternatives probe a predicted intermediate maximum between the measured 1/1 and 50/1 conditions.

m173 at 1/1 with DCM 1500 uL predicts 6.90/98.58; at 0/1 with DCM 2000 uL predicts 4.62/25.58 mL, both near 124.8 mg. The first tests whether the large measured 1/1 completion persists under a smaller plug; the second extends the fixed-setup solvent curve.

At their own measured loading setups, m216 at 2/1 predicts 13.30/24.74 and at 10/1 predicts 29.58/44.53; m146 at 2/1 predicts 15.41/29.94 mL. These distinguish interpolation from a local retention maximum. Cross-molecule interpretation remains confounded by loading-solvent identity.

Unmeasured pyridyl ketone m66 at 111.4 mg, DCM 300 uL: 2/1 predicts 6.51/14.06 and 5/1 predicts 11.47/27.18 mL. A matched solvent pair tests transfer from quinoline N to combined ring-N and carbonyl functionality.

Separate within-molecule tests: m91 at 20/1, 141.2 mg predicts 5.91/6.08; m82 at 20/1, 102.9 mg predicts 15.36/37.98 mL. Their injection setups match their respective measured anchors. The predicted interval collapse or earlier migration needs measurement.

Complementary transfer questions: unmeasured primary alcohol m204 at 5/1, 100.1 mg, PE 300 uL predicts 20.04/36.29; benzylic alcohol m67 at 5/1, 99.4 mg, DCM 300 uL predicts 10.31/16.38; m199 in pure EA at 100 mg, DCM 400 uL predicts 4.47/11.90 mL. m204 closely matches the m60/m61 protocol; m67 has a solvent confound; m199 isolates eluent change against its acquired 2/1 result.

chemistry_scientist.possible_model_blind_spots: GENERAL CHEMICAL KNOWLEDGE: increasing EA usually strengthens normal-phase elution; basic nitrogen, sulfoxide oxygen and accessible hydroxyls can interact strongly with silica. These priors motivate comparisons but do not explain the unusual labels by themselves. UNTESTED HYPOTHESES: graph-specific adsorption environments, conditional loading effects, dissolution and injection focusing contribute to the observed discrepancies. Shared HBD/HBA or TPSA totals cannot uniquely encode these distinctions. Current local maxima may reflect interpolation around new anchors, but their physical reality remains untested.
chemistry_scientist.coverage_or_redundancy_concerns: Distinct IDs frequently encode identical complete physical inputs, including measured inputs. Their value is replication when tied to a reproducibility question. Small density-derived mass differences should not be mistaken for substantial new coverage. Remaining ordinary aromatic, ester, ketone and aldehyde conditions provide complementary Row information; neither structural novelty nor extreme predicted retention alone establishes learning value.
warnings: V2 minus V1 is elution interval width, not uncertainty. Quantile widths also require ordering checks before interpretation.
Only observed-table IDs supply measured evidence. Current candidate predictions remain unmeasured even when their physical inputs match observed records.
Historical errors come from deliberately selected experiments. They establish those premeasurement failures, not overall Row accuracy or accuracy improvement after retraining.

m202 retains a formally positive phosphorus representation without a supplied counterion; confirm intended identity before applying a neutral-compound prior. The slightly reversed measured m195 interval in a917c928912c74862968 requires endpoint-definition awareness.

ml_scientist.state_summary: Seed 6101, free_llm32_dual_expert_v1, round 1: 365 observed records, including 32 newly acquired measurements; reported legal pool 2965; no pending records. The supplied catalog supports both targeted condition contrasts and broader graph coverage. Feedback strengthens evidence for scaffold-specific transfer errors and conditional endpoint responses. It weakens a general loading-induced widening rule and supports loading-solvent identity more strongly than plug volume. Current predictions have adapted around several newly measured graphs, while dose sensitivity remains nearly absent. No overall Row accuracy gain is established.
ml_scientist.important_observations:
MEASURED FEEDBACK AND HYPOTHESIS REVISIONS:
H_load remains supported only as a conditional response hypothesis. For m8 at 1/1, low/middle/high loading gives V1/V2 approximately 5.32/9.45, 4.23/11.45 and 4.22/13.04 mL (fd0fd67502640304b8fb; a98f3e4664fd05c0f82c; 6c4ddf5ad1cf067b81ee). At 5/1, low versus middle loading gives 5.74/11.29 versus 4.72/14.07 (c8176b3eea7a5d8802dc; 898bde0c214429571108). The m44 high-load repeat 61d5633c7221b3040a5f gives 7.76/20.25 versus the earlier 9.85/20.92, retaining earlier onset and later completion relative to low-load 11.88/17.52. Its onset differs between repeats by 2.09 mL.
A universal positive completion slope is contradicted by m92: at 1/1 with EA loading, increasing mass from 57.75 to 173.25 mg changes 5.18/12.01 to 6.29/9.73 (00a89de0e6cc7377a84b; 4451265787d29526a93a). At 50/1, the same mass increase changes 22.57/52.44 to 20.51/62.21 (1844eab177de5d01fab6; 9bbd36c8b484b5609808). At 10/1, middle-load completion 28.15 exceeds both low-load 21.03 and high-load 24.51. m101's measured completion increase is 0.73 mL at 2/1, versus 2.88 at 1/1. Smooth monotone loading curves and saturation mechanisms remain unestablished.
H_ratio splits into local questions. m173 completion is 108.89, 45.06 and 60.92 mL at 1/1, 2/1 and 5/1 with the same 2000 uL DCM setup (f90a5a5a54509c085ebd; 0b247863fd6e8aaf44d8; 1e775e7d8dcbf48fd6f8), indicating a recorded local trough. m73 intermediate onsets are 5.26 and 5.63 at 2/1 and 5/1, compared with 18.60 at 1/1; the late, narrow 1/1 interval is localized. m80's unusual completion response survives matching loading: 15.66 at 1/1 versus 8.27 at 50/1 at 105.5 mg (55dfd30fde788076a355; 08155ffdcb0d27576050). Its new premeasurement errors were below 0.07 mL for both endpoints.
H_onset is resolved at the tested condition: ce14dd2481560a984aea measured m177 at 10/1 and 140.6 mg as 5.20/20.70, versus the old prediction 0.00/31.74. The onset collapse was a prediction defect there.
H_nitrogen is supported for quinoline transfer, without supporting a generic nitrogen correction. At 5/1, m146 measured 37.67/59.83 and m216 31.43/56.33 (04a2e8ad27ca641a3a12; 1ae3618ec277b0463686), with premeasurement errors -27.84/-32.47 and -20.35/-28.90. In contrast, m160 at 2/1 measured 11.90/33.83 with errors +0.77/+0.56; its difference from the matched meta isomer is only +0.29/+2.26. Nitrogen accessibility as a causal explanation remains untested.
H_injection gains stronger support for solvent identity than plug volume. At fixed m92 mass, mobile phase and 200 uL plug, PE versus EA loading changes V1/V2 by +2.84/+8.56 (e626b5b8083ea1fd02f2; 00a89de0e6cc7377a84b). Reducing m173's DCM plug from 2000 to 1500 uL changes onset by -0.025 and completion by +1.16, with a 0.05 mg mass difference (0b247863fd6e8aaf44d8; 9a32b65bc21fdc5f7286). A general plug-volume effect remains weakly supported.
ml_scientist.important_model_behaviors:
CURRENT MODEL DIAGNOSTICS: Loading insensitivity persists after the connected loading program. At measured m92 10/1 inputs, candidates 0389a6366b3a51fad8b5 and ad0ace61c29817c678c2 predict completion 23.806 and 23.814 across a threefold mass increase, versus measured 21.033 and 24.513. At m101 1/1, db7eff29fb2c3ba5bcd3 and a37e31ac2c128f596cf6 predict a completion difference of about 0.010 versus measured 2.875. These comparisons diagnose training-input fit.
TRAJECTORY-LOCAL MODEL CHANGE: Still-eligible m216 candidate 33ffc69a253a89f15995 changed from approximately 11.08/27.42 to 30.30/50.71. m146 candidate 9e3ce3497298084abd83 changed from approximately 9.66/26.44 to 27.01/42.75. These substantial changes show adaptation around newly measured graphs; their unmeasured outcomes remain unknown.
MEASURED PREMEASUREMENT ERROR STRUCTURE: Errors are not a common endpoint offset. For m91 at 2/1, the old predicted band center was 6.95 versus measured 6.80, while predicted elution interval was 11.47 versus measured 2.36. m29 at 50/1 also combined too-early onset with too-late completion. Quinolines, m60 and m199 instead showed underprediction of both endpoints. Center and interval residuals distinguish these problems.
CURRENT QUANTILE DIAGNOSTICS: Crossings persist, although individual old defects changed. d997636736faa38ac83a has V1 q90=3.405 below q50=5.958 despite positive reported width 0.013. adbaa4b00d492d64eed5 has negative V1 width. ce39d1762993bbbafaca has V2 q10 above q50. Numerical width is not calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and point prediction and q50 provide redundant information.
ml_scientist.candidate_scientific_questions: Do quinoline responses change sharply between measured ratios, and do current weak-eluent declines persist? Does m91's corrected local response transfer beyond 5/1? Is m73's anomalous 1/1 interval reproducible? Does the measured loading-solvent contrast transfer to another familiar molecule? Can newly learned alcohol and beta-ketoester behavior transfer to related unseen graphs? These questions describe information value without defining a batch.
ml_scientist.possible_model_blind_spots: INFERENCES: Persistent flat dose predictions suggest weak condition-feature use or missing molecule-by-condition interactions. Strong graph-specific corrections alongside different endpoint-error signs argue against one global bias adjustment. A graph with similarity 1 can still have only one measured ratio. CHEMICAL/ML PRIORS: Adsorption accessibility, dissolution and injection conditions may explain some responses, but these mechanisms were not measured. Unusual recorded solvent curves prevent treating chemical monotonicity as truth.
ml_scientist.possible_learning_bottlenecks: Check numeric scaling, condition encoding, feature routing and output transformations using only the observed trajectory. More loading triplets may have low marginal value until the predictor can use their differences. ML prior: separate modeling or diagnostics of band center and elution interval, with molecule-by-condition interactions, could help capture opposing endpoint movements; improvement is unproven. Use grouped out-of-fold residual checks restricted to the 365 observed records, keeping exact-input replicates together. Separate graph transfer, ratio response, loading response and injection contrasts. Quantile-order repair alone would not establish calibration.
ml_scientist.coverage_or_redundancy_concerns:
Across the supplied pool, familiar aromatic compounds and repeated loading grids coexist with unseen pyridyl ketones, amino carbonyls, hydroxy esters, cyclic carbonyls and substituted aromatic families. The previous batch already supplied multiple labels for several difficult graphs; broader transferable support now complements unresolved local contrasts. Ordinary short and moderate retention examples remain relevant to the Row objective.
Group informational redundancy by molecule and all five condition fields. Many eligible IDs encode identical inputs or repeat observed inputs. Preserve catalog multiplicity when assessing Row representativeness, while discounting duplicate information. Different loads remain distinct experiments even when predictions coincide. m60, m181 and m199 now have molecule_novelty=0 and similarity 1 despite only one measured condition each. Binary condition novelty also poorly distinguishes interpolation from remote extrapolation. Further repeats need a specific ambiguity they could resolve.

ml_scientist.warnings: The 32 premeasurement residuals are prospective measured feedback for this acquisition, but the adaptively chosen batch is not an unbiased estimate of overall Row error. Repeated memory summaries are not additional measurements. historical_abs_error_ml equals the maximum absolute endpoint error in the supplied acquired examples; initial null errors are unavailable, not zero. Signed errors are prediction minus measurement. Elution interval V2 minus V1 is distinct from predictive quantile width. Only observed-table IDs supply measured outcomes; eligible duplicate inputs remain prediction-only records. Current fit to acquired labels does not establish retraining benefit. m195 observed a917c928912c74862968 has a slightly reversed interval, requiring endpoint-definition awareness. m202's positively charged phosphorus representation should be reconciled with intended experimental identity before interpreting a discrepancy through neutral-compound priors. No validation/test truth, future labels, other seeds or other methods were used.
